cards.surface: the face of the stone slab
cards.scene: a single slab of pale warm limestone fills the entire frame, seen straight on and flat, close enough that no edge of the slab is visible. the stone is old and softly veined with fine grey and umber marbling, faintly worn and chipped at a few points. a low raking warm light crosses the whole surface from one side. there is nothing else in the picture, no room, no objects, no background, only the stone.
cards.text_in: only one line of writing is cut into this stone, small and low down in the bottom third, reading exactly: hoganandcrownlaw.com, incised in plain letters. above it runs a long carved horizontal rule with tapered ends. the entire middle and upper half of the slab is left completely blank, clean unmarked stone with no writing and no carving of any kind in it. around the outer edges of the slab only, well away from the centre, are delicate carved embellishments: slender olive branches, small leaves and tight rosettes cut into the surface as relief. every groove is bare uncoloured stone, dark only from the shadow gathering inside the cut, with a hard bright edge along the side facing the light. no paint, no gilding, no colour inside any groove
